title: I love Connect Four, so I made a version where scoring can help your opponent
author: Jerome_bonjour
selftext:
I love Connect Four: simple rules, quick to pick up, and that feeling of setting a trap while the other person tries to spot it. But I wanted a version with more room for combinations, risks and comebacks. The first-player advantage also made me want to explore different rules.



That's where Pikon came from. You still line up four tokens, but an alignment scores points and disappears. The tokens above fall, potentially creating new alignments for either player.



A move can score immediately and still be a bad move: the cascade might give your opponent even more points. You have to think about the board you'll leave behind, and whether to take points now or set up a better combination.



I wanted to keep the simplicity of Connect Four while giving each move more consequences.



On the AI side, I made the cinematic trailer with Dola/Seedance, using the game's character and board art as references. I generated six shots separately and assembled them in HyperFrames, cutting one boat shot short when it started inventing an extra character.



Trailer: [https://youtu.be/fCEeUwPyv9U](https://youtu.be/fCEeUwPyv9U)

Game (iOS / Android): [https://pikon.web.app/get](https://pikon.web.app/get)



If you try a few rounds, I'd love to know: did you have fun? Did the cascades give you interesting decisions and make you want another round, or did something get in the way?
